# Welcome to PS50008A {background-color="#275882"}

## Research Methods & Experimental Design {.center}

Term 2 | Spring 2026

---

## What is This Module About?

::: {.objectives-box}
**You will learn to:**

- **Design** experiments that can answer your questions
- **Analyse** data using R
- **Interpret** results appropriately
- **Report** findings in professional APA format
:::

---

## Why Research Methods?

Psychology is a **science**.

To make claims about human behaviour, we need:

- Systematic observation
- Controlled experiments
- Statistical analysis
- Peer review

This module teaches you the **tools** to do this.

---

# The Data Olympics {background-color="#275882"}

## Thursday: Your First Session

::: {.callout-important}
## No Lecture This Week
Your first contact is **Thursday's lab session** (10:00-12:00).

There is no Monday lecture in Week 11.
:::

---

## What Are the Data Olympics?

A series of **6 cognitive task stations** where you:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Test reaction times
- Complete memory tasks
- Make estimations
- Rate your confidence
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Work in pairs
- Record data in Qualtrics
- Experience being a participant
- Experience being a tester
:::
::::

---

## Why "Olympics"?

The data you generate becomes our **teaching dataset**.

When we learn about:

| Topic | Your Data |
|-------|-----------|
| Distributions | Your reaction times |
| t-tests | Room A vs Room B |
| Correlations | Memory vs confidence |

...we use [**your**]{.inverse-box} data, not abstract examples.

---

## The 6 Stations

::: {.step-1}
**1. Simple Reaction Time** — How fast can you respond to a stimulus?
:::

::: {.step-2}
**2. Choice Reaction Time** — How does decision-making affect speed?
:::

::: {.step-3}
**3. Memory Task** — How many items can you recall?
:::

---

## The 6 Stations (continued)

::: {.step-1}
**4. Estimation Task** — How accurate are your judgments?
:::

::: {.step-2}
**5. Group Estimation** — Does group discussion improve accuracy?
:::

::: {.step-3}
**6. Confidence Ratings** — How well do you know what you know?
:::

---

# What You Need to Know {background-color="#275882"}

## Before Thursday

::: {.callout-tip}
## Preparation Checklist
1. Check your lab allocation (Group A or Group B)
2. Bring your phone or laptop (for Qualtrics)
3. Arrive on time — we need to start promptly at 10:00
:::

---

## Form Your Project Groups

By the end of Thursday, form groups of [**3-4 students**]{.inverse-box}.

Your group will:

- Work together on the **research project**
- Conduct labs together from **Week 16**
- Generate data for the **Research Report**

::: {.callout-note}
## Choose Wisely
Pick people you can reliably meet with outside class.
:::
